classification.difficultyReason: Link substitution, a value table, ordered pairs and a graph; choose suitable axis scales from the calculated ranges and check collinearity.

content.prompt: For each given rule, complete the table, list the coordinates of the points, and plot the points on the Cartesian plane. (After you have completed the table, decide on the scale of your axes.) Check the points are collinear.

answer.worked:
Multiply each supplied $x$-value by $4$:
$$\begin{align*}y(-3)&=4(-3)=-12\\y(-2)&=4(-2)=-8\\y(-1)&=4(-1)=-4\\y(0)&=4(0)=0\\y(1)&=4(1)=4\\y(2)&=4(2)=8\\y(3)&=4(3)=12\end{align*}$$
The coordinate pairs are $(-3,-12),(-2,-8),(-1,-4),(0,0),(1,4),(2,8),(3,12)$. Use a horizontal scale of $1$ unit per square and a vertical scale of $2$ units per square. Plot each point by moving horizontally first, then vertically. A straightedge passes through all seven points, so they are collinear.

spec.description: Seven discrete plotted points; unit horizontal grid and two-unit vertical grid. Coordinate labels are supplied in the editable answer text.

Take the opposite of each supplied $x$-value:
$$\begin{align*}y(-3)&=-(-3)=3\\y(-2)&=-(-2)=2\\y(-1)&=-(-1)=1\\y(0)&=-(0)=0\\y(1)&=-(1)=-1\\y(2)&=-(2)=-2\\y(3)&=-(3)=-3\end{align*}$$
The coordinate pairs are $(-3,3),(-2,2),(-1,1),(0,0),(1,-1),(2,-2),(3,-3)$. Use $1$ unit per square on both axes. Plot horizontally first, then vertically. A straightedge passes through all seven points, so they are collinear.
